strube_edition: Strube 1928, Oliver Ditson (scan: references/The Theory and Use of Chords.pdf)
strube_wording_paraphrase: In strict writing two voices must not progress simultaneously in fifths (p. 9); guard against parallel fifths (p. 12, Fig. 30).
exceptions_stated_by_strube: Consecutive fifths in contrary motion are not objectionable (p. 9, Fig. 21); parallel fifths acceptable when the second is not perfect (p. 35); diminished-to-perfect fifths only when passing, i.e. no change of harmonic function (pp. 34-35); no objectionable fifths at a chord repetition (p. 35); retarded fifths produced by a suspension may be written (p. 83); fifths between IV and II harmless but avoided for now (p. 45)
decision: Measured: perfect-to-perfect fifths by similar motion. Not measured (needs harmonic analysis): passing d5-P5, chord repetition, suspension-produced fifths.
notes: Page numbers are printed book pages; PDF page = book page + 6 in the early chapters.

strube_edition: Strube 1928, Oliver Ditson (scan: references/The Theory and Use of Chords.pdf)
strube_wording_paraphrase: Forbidden to progress simultaneously in unisons or octaves; parallel octaves or unisons never sound bad but are inappropriate when the four voices are to be kept distinct (p. 9); guard against parallel octaves and unisons (p. 12).
exceptions_stated_by_strube: Contrary motion not objectionable (p. 9); holding two voices on an octave or unison is permissible because parallels arise only by motion (p. 23); retarded octaves produced by a suspension should be avoided (p. 83)
decision: Measured: octaves/unisons by similar motion, including compound octaves.

strube_edition: Strube 1928, Oliver Ditson (scan: references/The Theory and Use of Chords.pdf)
strube_wording_paraphrase: The soprano may be as far as an octave from the alto (occasionally even farther), but alto and tenor should only transiently be separated to such an extent; the bass may lie anywhere within its range (p. 20). Close, open, and no mixed position (p. 7).
exceptions_stated_by_strube: S-A occasionally farther than an octave (p. 20)
decision: Measured: S-A or A-T interval > 12 semitones at an event. Strube's close/open/mixed-position rule (p. 7) needs chord identity and is not measured.
notes: Strube softens S-A; the flag marks departure from the stated norm.

strube_edition: Strube 1928, Oliver Ditson (scan: references/The Theory and Use of Chords.pdf)
strube_wording_paraphrase: If an occasional crossing of the parts (not over the soprano) yields a better voice-leading, it should be used (chorale harmonization chapter).
exceptions_stated_by_strube: Crossing of lower parts allowed occasionally (p. 174)
decision: Measured: any of A, T, B sounding above the soprano at an event. Crossings among A, T, B are not counted.
notes: Narrower than Yan category 10 (all crossings), following Strube.

strube_edition: Strube 1928, Oliver Ditson (scan: references/The Theory and Use of Chords.pdf)
strube_wording_paraphrase: Overlapping occurs when two neighbouring voices are led so that the lower one progresses to a tone higher than that of the upper voice in the preceding chord, and vice versa; use it for the present only when one voice moves stepwise (p. 12, Figs. 32-33).
exceptions_stated_by_strube: Allowed when one voice moves stepwise (p. 12); Fig. 33 marks the both-skip case 'avoid' (p. 13)
decision: Measured: overlap between adjacent voices, not crossed at the new event, with neither voice moving by 1-2 semitones.
notes: 'For the present' qualifier noted; no later relaxation found in the scanned pages.
